summary: A small craft-and-art community in San Kamphaeng, best approached as a slow browse through Loang Him Kao’s workshops, cafés and shops, with Chamcha Market as its weekend focal point. Worth the trip if you want to meet makers and browse locally made goods; the market itself is short and seasonal schedules should be checked close to travel.
whyGo: More intimate than a large city market: the village has craft shops, cafés, textiles and embroidery, while weekend Chamcha Market brings together maker stalls, food and drinks beneath a rain tree.
A convenient pairing with the Bo Sang craft area on the east side of Chiang Mai.
bestFor: Craft and textile browsing, relaxed café stops, and visitors who enjoy small community markets.
A half-day outing that can be combined with other San Kamphaeng sights.
skipIf: You are only free on a weekday and expect a lively market: the weekend market is the main draw, and individual weekday shops vary.
You need a fully step-free, reliably accessible site or a major attraction with extensive indoor exhibits.
duration: Allow 1–2 hours to browse the market and village; plan a half-day if adding a meal, workshop or Bo Sang. This is a planning estimate, not a published visit duration.
cost: No admission charge is listed by the tourism source. Food, drinks and crafts are paid directly to vendors; prices vary. Workshop availability and prices need to be confirmed with the individual maker.
hours: Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) lists Chamcha Market on Saturdays and Sundays, 09:00–14:30. The wider village has varied shop hours: TAT lists typical weekend hours of 09:00–15:00 and weekday hours of 10:00–17:00. Check current operator notices before setting out.
bestTime: Go near opening on a Saturday or Sunday for the fullest market and cooler conditions; arriving before noon leaves time to browse and eat before the listed 14:30 close.
gettingThere: In San Klang, San Kamphaeng, east of Chiang Mai. TAT gives about 20 minutes by car from the Old City; another TAT village listing estimates about 25 minutes from Tha Phae Gate. Use Chamcha Market as the map destination, since the village name may not resolve. A taxi or ride-hail is the simplest option; confirm the return pickup in advance. Journey times vary with traffic.
booking: No booking is indicated for browsing the market. Contact the market or an individual shop in advance for current opening, special events or workshops. TAT lists Chamcha Market’s Facebook page and phone +66 97 462 4296.
accessibility: No reliable accessibility details found. Expect an outdoor village/market with walking between shops; surface quality, step-free access, accessible toilets and seating are unverified. Contact the venue before travel if these are essential.
practicalTips: Check the Chamcha Market Facebook page shortly before your chosen weekend; listings differ slightly on closing time and special events may change the schedule.
Carry cash for small purchases and ask before photographing makers, workspaces or residents.
Keep the return ride in mind: do not assume a taxi will be waiting in this suburban area.
decemberNotes: December 2026 weekends fall on 5–6, 12–13, 19–20 and 26–27 December. The regular Saturday/Sunday schedule is the best planning assumption, but holiday closures and any special December fair have not been announced in the sources checked. Confirm the exact weekend close to travel; no specific 2026 December event is verified.
uncertainties: Market hours vary by source (TAT lists 09:00–14:30; other recent tourism and local guides list 09:00–14:00 or 09:00–15:00). Use 14:00 as a prudent arrival cutoff and verify directly.
Transport fares, live availability, accessibility, workshop schedules and exact December holiday operations are not published in the sources used.
The referenced image is an illustrative market photo on TAT’s Chamcha Market page; image reuse permission and photographer credit are not established.
